title: Datasette links agent-built apps to local models, with permission fixes to apply
summary: Agent 0.6a0, Apps 0.4a0 and datasette-llm 0.1a11 add linked app views, a homepage prompt and directly configured model endpoints, including local ones. Datasette 1.0a43 also fixes private stored-query disclosure; its scope differs from the separate download-permission fix in 0.65.6.

sections.title: Linked apps and local-model configuration arrive
sections.html:
November 14–15 releases extend Datasette’s database-to-app workflow: Agent 0.6a0 adds a homepage chat prompt, Apps 0.4a0 lets apps link to specific views in one another, and datasette-llm 0.1a11 supports directly configured OpenAI-compatible endpoints. The latter includes unauthenticated local endpoints, so a provider API key is no longer a universal prerequisite. Tool-calling capability remains necessary.

The panel beside chat and explicit query grants introduced in Agent 0.5a0 and Apps 0.3a0 remain useful context. The new releases are prereleases. This update also examines Datasette 1.0a43 permission fixes; no installation or native execution was performed. The original report date and identity are preserved.

Datasette Apps 0.4a0 release · Datasette Agent 0.6a0 release

sections.title: References and links connect reviewed apps
sections.html:
The agent panel lets people discuss a database-backed interface while viewing it. Permission-checked # references attach tables, databases or stored queries. Apps can supply references without exposing their HTML: reading source through app_view requires edit permission.

Apps 0.4a0 adds fragment-based view state, including bookmarks, reloads and browser back/forward navigation. An app can advertise supported links through a manifest; the agent’s app_links tool lists links from apps the current user can view. A search app can therefore open a specific record in a separate detail app. The app_debug tool accepts a hash for checking that view.

Fragments are inputs, not permission grants. The current README warns that apps should not write data simply because a fragment loaded. Agent 0.6a0 also asks before opening panel links to other sites and blocks panel forms that submit elsewhere. These documented boundaries do not establish generated-interface correctness.

Datasette Apps 0.4a0 release

sections.title: Approval and cancellation retain specific boundaries
sections.html:
The Agent README describes write SQL as an ordered sequence analyzed before explicit chat approval. Execution uses the requesting actor’s permissions. If a statement fails, later statements are skipped while earlier successes remain committed. Review SQL, parameters and affected records before approval.

The 0.5a0 Stop behavior preserves streamed text and stops before the next step; an already-started tool finishes. Navigating away does not stop the conversation. Neither action rolls back writes. The existing app-query grant workflow likewise controls access rather than proving that a query calculates the intended answer.

Agent 0.6a0 fixes sending each user message twice. It also stops an existing conversation if its selected model becomes blocked, leaves the allowlist or loses its required key, asking for a new chat. Model selection remains pinned for a conversation.

Datasette Agent 0.6a0 release

sections.title: Local endpoints change the access requirement
sections.html:
datasette-llm 0.1a11 accepts endpoint dictionaries containing api_base, with a local model identifier and separate model_name for the remote server. It supports Chat Completions or Responses endpoints without an additional LLM plugin. Endpoint models advertise tools and streaming by default; verify that the actual server and chosen model implement them.

An endpoint without key is unauthenticated and never receives a provider’s default credential. With an explicit key name, lookup checks datasette-secrets and then LLM’s stored keys. A missing named key raises an error rather than falling back. The release warns against putting credentials in extra headers because those appear in the configuration endpoint.

Allowlists and blocklists now apply to explicit model lookups and defaults, not only model listing. Apps 0.4a0 requires Datasette 1.0a42 or later, but affected private-query deployments need the 1.0a43 fix. Record the entire installed combination; minimum dependency versions alone do not establish a tested or appropriately patched setup.

datasette-llm 0.1a11 release

sections.title: Apply permission fixes alongside the app update
sections.html:
GHSA-mw6v-83vp-7c4c affects Datasette 1.0a31–1.0a42 and is patched in 1.0a43. The owner_id filter could expose another user’s private stored-query name, title, description and SQL, including to anonymous clients who knew or guessed the actor ID. The advisory says this does not itself allow query execution, editing, deletion or access to otherwise forbidden tables. Instances need saved private queries to be affected; stable 0.65.x has no stored queries and is unaffected by this advisory.

A separate database-download permission issue concerns databases whose configured route differs from their name. Its fix appears in 1.0a43 and stable 0.65.6; permission hooks must check the database name. Do not conflate that condition with stored-query disclosure.

Managed HTML apps remain sandboxed with app-scoped query grants and actor permissions. External HTTPS origins require configuration. Python plugin apps are unrestricted by that HTML sandbox. An allowed query or origin does not guarantee sound SQL, harmless code or appropriate data disclosure.

Private stored-query disclosure advisory · Datasette 0.65.6 release

sections.title: Keep the answer checkable across linked views
sections.html:
For a teaching lab, prepare an attributable SQLite dataset and instructor-written answer key. Connect a permitted model, tag a table, inspect a proposed query, and build a search app linked to record details. Check known answers, empty results, missing values and browser back navigation. Include a forbidden record to verify that neither a guessed fragment nor a link grants access. Local inference changes hosting choices, not the need to check answers.

For a collection website, preserve reviewed stored queries and app source. Test links as the intended visitor, including keyboard use, loading failures and removed query grants. Review whether a schema change or model-generated revision silently omits records. Hosting, permissions, endpoint configuration and accessibility remain integration work.

A narrated video can show a question, its SQL and the corresponding linked record side by side. Record the dataset version and visible filters so the demonstration remains interpretable. These teaching, website and video workflows are proposals, not tested outcomes.

sections.title: A bounded evaluation remains appropriate
sections.html:
The inspected Agent and Apps licenses are Apache 2.0; dataset and model-service rights remain separate. The update makes linked interfaces and local endpoints more practical to investigate while tightening several configuration paths. It does not establish production readiness, compatibility with every local model, lower cost or better learning outcomes.

Start with small acceptance data and recorded package versions. Confirm that excluded models and forbidden queries fail as intended, and that app revisions preserve previously correct results. Primary tagged notes and the security advisory were inspected; README observations are dated November 18 and may describe development beyond those tags. No exploit, benchmark or live-provider test was run.

useCases: Teacher-reviewed database exploration with a checkable answer key
A searchable collection website built from reviewed stored queries
limitations: Agent, Apps, datasette-llm and Datasette 1.0a43 are prereleases; stable 0.65.6 addresses a separate database-download issue.
No installation, native app execution, exploit, compatibility test, benchmark or live provider/local-model test was performed.
Current README observations are dated November 18 and may extend beyond tagged releases.
Endpoint tools/streaming defaults do not verify that a configured server or model supports those capabilities.
Stop is not rollback, actor/query permissions do not guarantee SQL correctness, and the HTML sandbox does not restrict Python plugin apps.
The stored-query advisory exposes metadata and SQL text under stated conditions; it does not itself allow execution or otherwise unauthorized table access.
Apache 2.0 covers the inspected Agent/Apps code; data and model-service rights remain separate.

judgment: A useful incremental update for existing Datasette datasets: test linked apps and local-model access on small acceptance data, with patched permissions and recorded versions. The alpha releases and untested generated results still limit adoption confidence.
researchNote: Stable report revised from six freshly captured primary tagged release/advisory pages, four current Agent/Apps README/license captures, the earlier Agent 0.5a0 release reread and author release posts. Public HTTP/parser acquisition followed a Chrome timeout. Existing architectural context was rechecked where used; no native execution, exploit or independent experimental validation was performed. Use cases remain editorial proposals.
